New!
  

 This integration is available exclusively through Smily!



💡 What is PAP Vacances?

PAP Vacances is a French's No. 1 classified ad site featuring 25,000 listings across Europe and 92 million page views per year.
You can now publish your properties and receive instant bookings through Smily, reaching over 1 million unique monthly visitors on the PAP Vacances website.


 🔐 Key Benefits

Differentiate yourself from competition thanks to this integration only available on Smily.
You can choose your pricing model to be on commission or on an annual fee per listing. Or even use both depending on properties!
Increase your direct bookings ! You process the bookings and you own the traveller information so you can retarget them for their next holiday and convert them into loyal customers!
Reach a new niche of french travellers.



 🤑 Flexible Pricing


12% commission (including taxes) on your bookings
OR an annual per-property payment model with 0% commission

 🔄 How Does It Work?

Your properties go live on PAP Vacances, and you start receiving bookings!
For more details on PAP and a step-by-step setup guide, check out this article.

Download the app

💌 Any question?

If you have any questions or would like to learn more, reach out to smily@pap.fr
articles.title: Publish your listings on PAP Vacances ! 🔥 Only available with Smily

Scheduled - Changelog [published Oct 16]: https://developer.airbnb.com/changelog/changes-to-step-free-guest-entrance-feature
To streamline the step-free entrance accessibility feature, "Step-free path to the guest entrance" will be removed and combined with "Step-free guest entrance”, for one simplified feature called "Step-free access”. 
We will automatically update listings to only use the "Step-free access" accessibility feature. The migration begins on November 5, 2024 and lasts approximately one month. During this period, the submission of both accessibility features will be temporarily disabled. On December 5, 2024, the submission of home_step_free_access ("Step-free access") will be re-enabled.
Learn more: https://developer.airbnb.com/changelog/changes-to-step-free-guest-entrance-feature

During the above window, our Engineering team will be performing maintenance on redundant upstream electrical systems in order to improve reliability in our AMS3 region.
Expected Impact:
Power systems are redundant and we don’t expect to see any downtime, however, in the very unlikely situation that we lose power to both supplies, users may experience disruption with the following services or for a brief period:
Networking
Backups
Snapshots
Droplet create & restore operations
We will endeavor to keep any downtime to a minimum for the duration of the change.
If you have any questions related to this issue please send us a ticket from your cloud support page. https://cloudsupport.digitalocean.com/s/createticket
Thank you,
Team DigitalOcean

articles.description:
Incident began at 2024-11-19 18:44 and ended at 2024-11-19 20:24 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Mini Incident Report

We apologize for the inconvenience this service disruption/outage may have caused. We would like to provide some information about this incident below. Please note, this information is based on our best knowledge at the time of posting and is subject to change as our investigation continues. If you have experienced impact outside of what is listed below, please reach out to Google Workspace Support using help article https://support.google.com/a/answer/1047213.

(All Times US/Pacific)

Incident Start: 19 November 2024 10:44

Incident End: 19 November 2024 12:24

Duration: 1 hour, 40 minutes

Affected Services and Features:

Google Calendar

Regions/Zones: Global

Description:

Google Calendar experienced service issues, preventing some web users from accessing their calendars for a duration of 1 hour, 40 minutes. From preliminary analysis, the root cause of the issue was a misconfigured traffic management rule that incorrectly blocked legitimate traffic.

Google engineers mitigated impact by rolling back the misconfigured traffic management rule that was blocking legitimate traffic.

Google will complete a full IR in the following days that will provide a full root cause.

Customer Impact:

The issue affected Google Calendar Web users and was triggered when users attempted to transfer calendar event ownership. Once this happened, one or more users were unable to access any part of their calendar through the website.

Calendar mobile application users were not affected.

Affected products: Google Calendar
articles.title:
RESOLVED: **Summary:**
Google Calendar experienced service issues, preventing some web users from accessing their calendars.
**Description:**
On November 19, 2024, between 10:44 AM and 12:24 PM US/Pacific, a subset of Google Calendar users encountered problems accessing the Calendar web UI.
We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused our valued customers.
**Diagnosis:**
The issue affected Google Calendar Web users and was triggered when users attempted to transfer a calendar event ownership. Once this happened, one or more users were unable to access any part of their calendar through the website.
The issue did not affect the Calendar mobile application
**Workaround:**
There were no workarounds at the time of the issue

Oct 30, 09:42 UTC
Resolved - On October 30, 2024, between 5:45 and 9:42 UTC, the Actions service was degraded, causing run delays. On average, Actions workflow run, job, and step updates were delayed as much as one hour. The delays were caused by updates in a dependent service that led to failures in Redis connectivity. Delays recovered once the Redis cluster connectivity was restored at 8:16 UTC. The incident was fully mitigated once the job queue had processed by 9:24 UTC. This incident followed an earlier short period of impact on hosted runners due to a similar issue, which was mitigated by failing over to a healthy cluster.
From this, we are working to improve our observability across Redis clusters to reduce our time to detection and mitigation of issues like this one in the future where multiple clusters and services were impacted.  We will also be working to reduce the time to mitigate and improve general resilience to this dependency.

articles.title: Incident: Error associated with adding steps to workflows

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From around 7:00 AM PST to 8:30 AM PST on November 14, some users may have experienced minor delays using Slack.

Initially, we believed that there may have been widespread user impact and our updates reflected this. During our investigation, however, we confirmed that most user impact was mitigated by our automatic retry mechanisms and load balancers.

A scheduled upgrade added unanticipated load to some parts of our infrastructure. This caused a small spike in errors across our systems. As an immediate mitigation step, we rolled back this planned change. We completed the rollback at 8:30AM PST on November 14, which resolved the issue for all affected customers. 

The databases that had already picked up the change required restarts. We then carefully shepherded the database fleet through rolling restarts, resolving all errors by 1:00 AM PST November 15. Although user impact had already been mitigated, we continued sharing updates until this process was completed.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be having trouble sending messages, files, loading threads and channels.

articles.description:
Between approximately 12:35 PM PST on November 11, 2024, and 10:05 PM PST on November 12, 2024, users may have experienced some channels missing from their default section in their sidebar.

This issue was initially handled as a bug report, but due to the widespread impact on end users, we enacted our incident response processes. Through our investigation, we traced the problem to an issue with backend code logic. This code was incorrectly categorizing these conversations as App/Integration DMs, resulting in these conversations being moved to an incorrect location in the users' sidebar.

To resolve the issue, we reverted the problematic code, restoring affected channel destinations in the sidebar.

*We adjusted this summary's impact start time to reflect more accurately, we apologize for any confusion.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with the channel list

articles.description:
From 12:02 AM PDT to 1:19 AM PDT on Sunday, November 3, 2024, some users experienced trouble logging into Slack with SSO, provisioning users with SCIM, received duplicated notifications, and had trouble triggering workflows.

The system responsible for the handling of database replications and routing traffic had unexpected failures due to a time-logic configuration change. As a result, requests involving these database replicas timed out, impacting all SCIM operations, SSO logins, notification handling, and workflow execution.

As an immediate fix, we manually processed these database replications, restoring full functionality to the affected services. 

After verifying that requests were successfully serviced, we implemented a backend logic update to allow for future system changes to be handled automatically, reducing the likelihood of this reoccurring.
articles.title: Incident: Users unable to sign in with SSO or SCIM. Multiple Slack features are experiencing issues.

articles.description:
From October 31, 2024 4:30 PM PDT to November 1, 2024 3:30 AM PDT some users experienced issues with the date field in lists appearing garbled. 

We were able to trace this back to a code change that inadvertently caused the issue.

We reverted this code change which resolved the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with the date field in lists

articles.description:
From approximately 4:11 PM PDT to 4:13 PM PDT on Wednesday, October 30, 2024, some users experienced issues with essential functions like loading, connecting, and sending messages in Slack.

A recent backend change was intended to improve traffic and error handling. However, an unexpected configuration change during the rollout led to a temporary spike in connection errors.

We observed automatic recovery from the configuration change, which restored functionality to affected users. However, we reverted the problematic code that initially caused the issue.
articles.title: Incident: Connectivity issues in Slack

articles.description:
On Monday, October 28, 2024 around 2:29 PM PDT until 6:55 PM PDT, some users observed workflows containing steps that included some connectors such as Google Sheets, Slack lists, or Jira could not be saved.

We discovered there were missing components from a recent feature release causing the inability to save workflow steps. We adjusted the backend logic to include the missing components, restoring full functionality to affected workflow steps.
articles.title: Incident: Some workflows are unable to be saved.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From 3:19 PM PDT to around 4:02 PM PDT on October 24, 2024, lists were unavailable in Slack. Users may have come up against an error message or noticed that the feature was missing from the sidebar.

We accidentally deactivated the lists feature during the course of routine cleanup work. Once we realised this mistake, we immediately re-enabled lists for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Lists are unavailable for users

articles.description:
On October 15, 2024, from 12:00 PM PDT to 2:33 PM PDT, some workflows that utilize incoming webhooks to send messages returned the error “team_not_found”, and the messages weren’t shared to the intended channel.

We traced the issue back to a recent code change related to ensuring webhooks and plugins work as expected. The change didn’t account for a variable, which triggered the error.

Once we reverted the change and rolled out a fix, the issue was resolved for all affected workflows.
articles.title: Incident: Some webhooks are returning `team_not_found`
